## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

Five independent bearers, none following from another — each is the
caller that already makes the call and would carry the fix:

- `PreparationViewModel` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/preparation/PreparationViewModel.kt, `onLaunchClicked`
- `ControlViewModel` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/control/ControlViewModel.kt, `onUndoClicked` and `onStopConfirmed`
- `ImportPreviewViewModel` — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/ui/importpreview/ImportPreviewViewModel.kt, `onSaveClicked`
- `RaceDetailViewModel` — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/ui/racedetail/RaceDetailViewModel.kt, `onDeleteConfirmed` and `onRenameConfirmed`
- `ProfileSyncPushService` — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sync/ProfileSyncPushService.kt, `push` and `applyIncoming`

## Trigger

- "Lancer" tapped on the preparation screen, both the `Ready` and the

- The undo pill tapped (`onUndoClicked`) and "Arrêter" confirmed

- "Enregistrer" tapped on the import preview screen (`onSaveClicked`) — observed

## Today

`PreparationViewModel.onLaunchClicked` calls
`raceLaunchController.launch(startedAt, startedAtElapsedRealtime)` in the
`Ready` branch and `raceLaunchController.retryAndLaunch(...)` in the
`OpenFailed` branch. Both return `Result<Race>` (from
`RaceRecordingRepository.startClock` through `RaceLaunchController`),
and both are called for their side effect only — `navigator.launchRace()`
runs unconditionally right after, whether the clock started or not.

`ControlViewModel.onUndoClicked` calls
`undoMarkingController.undo(heldRace.id)`, a `Result<Race>`, and chains
`.onSuccess { ... }` with no `.onFailure` — a failed undo leaves
`heldRace` and the UI exactly as before, with nothing said.
`onStopConfirmed` calls `stopRaceController.stop(heldRace.id, atInstant)`,
also a `Result`, and likewise only chains `.onSuccess { ... }` — a
failed stop leaves the confirmation dialog open with no error shown and
no branch that reports it.

`ImportPreviewViewModel.onSaveClicked` calls
`raceRepository.saveImportedRace(...)`, a `Result<Race>`, and chains
`.onSuccess { race -> navigator.toRaceDetailAfterImport(race.id) }`
with no failure branch: on failure the method returns having done
nothing visible — the screen stays as it is, and the user has no way to
tell the import was not saved.

`RaceDetailViewModel.onDeleteConfirmed` calls
`raceRepository.delete(raceId)`, checks `result.isSuccess` and calls
`navigator.back()` only then — on failure nothing runs, including no
reset of `dialogState.isDeleteConfirmVisible`, so the confirmation
stays open with no message. `onRenameConfirmed` calls
`raceRepository.rename(raceId, name)` and never reads the returned
`Result` at all — its contract (`RaceRepository.kt`) says it refuses an
empty trimmed name or one past 40 characters, leaving the stored name
unchanged; the caller always runs
`dialogState.value = dialogState.value.copy(renameFieldValue = null)`
right after, closing the dialog regardless, so a refused rename looks
identical to a successful one and the old name silently stays.

`ProfileSyncPushService.push` calls
`profileRepository.markSyncSuccess(at)` at line 39, right after a
confirmed delivery, and returns `ProfileSyncPushOutcome.Success`
without checking that call's own `Result<Unit>`.
`ProfileSyncPushService.applyIncoming` calls the same
`profileRepository.markSyncSuccess(at)` at line 66, after every write
above it has succeeded, and returns `ProfileSyncApplyOutcome.Applied`
the same way, dropping the `Result` — unlike every other write in this
same method (`replaceReference`, the five calls inside `applyProfile`),
which are all checked with `.isFailure`.

No file in the project defines a rejection or failure message resource
for any of these seven call sites — `PhoneStringResources` carries
`hrMaxRejected`, `distanceRejected`, `pressDurationRejected` and
`zoneThresholdRejected` for `ProfileViewModel`'s own four setting
handlers, and nothing equivalent for launch, undo, stop, import-save,
delete or rename; `WatchStringResources` carries no rejection or
failure text at all.

## Expected

Each of the seven call sites reads the `Result` it already receives (or,
for `applyIncoming`'s and `push`'s `markSyncSuccess`, starts reading it)
and acts on a failure the way `ProfileViewModel` already does on its own
four setting handlers — surfacing a rejection distinctly from doing
nothing, rather than treating the call as fire-and-forget:

- `PreparationViewModel.onLaunchClicked` only calls
  `navigator.launchRace()` when `launch`/`retryAndLaunch` returns a
  success; a failure is surfaced on the preparation screen instead of
  leaving it for a race that never started.
- `ControlViewModel.onUndoClicked` and `onStopConfirmed` add a failure
  branch alongside their existing `.onSuccess`, each surfacing that its
  action did not go through.
- `ImportPreviewViewModel.onSaveClicked` surfaces a failure on the
  import preview screen instead of silently doing nothing.
- `RaceDetailViewModel.onDeleteConfirmed` surfaces a failure instead of
  leaving the confirmation open unexplained.
  `onRenameConfirmed` reads `rename`'s `Result` and, on failure — an
  empty or over-length trimmed name — keeps the dialog open (or
  otherwise says the name was refused) instead of closing it and
  discarding the input silently.
- `ProfileSyncPushService.push` and `applyIncoming` check
  `markSyncSuccess`'s `Result` the way every other write in
  `applyIncoming` already is, and report their own failure outcome
  (`ProfileSyncPushOutcome.Failure` / `ProfileSyncApplyOutcome.Failure`)
  instead of `Success`/`Applied` when it fails.

Each of these five bearers needs its own rejection or failure text —
none exists today, on either app's resource catalogue, for launch,
undo, stop, import-save, delete or rename.
